nodes.notes: PROBLEM: MoE with B=1,S=16,D=32,I=32,E=8,top_k=1. Tiny dims, very few tokens. (1) Classification: mixed (gate matmul + softmax + topk + permutation + per-expert SwiGLU MLP + scatter). (2) Canonical math: y[n] = w[n]*(SiLU(x[n]@W1[e[n]].T) * (x[n]@W3[e[n]].T)) @ W2[e[n]].T, where e[n]=argmax(softmax(gate(x[n]))), w[n]=max prob. With top_k=1, no scatter conflicts. (3) Layout: x:(16,32) fp16 contig; W1,W2,W3:(8,32,32) fp16 contig; gate.weight:(8,32). All weights total ~50KB — fits easily in shared/L1. (4) Regimes: a) tiny N (here) — latency bound by launches; b) larger N — compute bound on per-expert matmul; c) very large N — bandwidth bound on weight loads. (5) Knobs: full fusion vs split; block-per-token vs block-per-expert; precompute expert assignment; skip the sort entirely since top_k=1 (just gather per token). (6) Skeleton: Phase1 compute gate scores + softmax + argmax per token in one kernel; Phase2 fused SwiGLU MLP per token using its assigned expert weights. (7) Family A: FULL FUSION single kernel — one program per token, load token, compute gate scores, softmax, argmax, then run full MLP using that expert's weights — eliminates all intermediate global writes and the sort. Best for tiny N. Family B: Two-kernel (gate kernel + MoE MLP kernel) — simpler. Family C: Per-expert kernel like reference but fused per expert — worst (many launches). NOTE: with top_k=1 sort is unnecessary — each token writes to its own output row, no scatter conflict.

action.description: Single Triton kernel: one program per token. Each program loads its token (D=32), computes gate logits against all 8 experts, applies softmax+argmax to get expert id and weight, then performs SwiGLU MLP (W1, W3, W2 matmuls with SiLU) using only that expert's weights, multiplies by the top-1 weight, and writes the output row directly. Skip the sort/scatter entirely since top_k=1 means each token has a unique output row.
action.rationale: Tiny problem dominated by launch overhead. Full fusion to a single kernel eliminates ~10+ launches and all intermediate allocations. Per-token program keeps register/shared usage minimal.

nodes.notes: CURRENT: does=Single-program-per-2-tokens fused MoE; loads gate once, then per-token computes softmax, picks top-1 expert, runs w1/w3 GEMV+SiLU*up, then w2 GEMV, scales by gate prob. bottleneck=latency/launch + long_scoreboard global loads (weights). FOLLOW_THROUGH: aligned_with_intent=yes; packed 2 tokens/program via TOKENS_PER_PROG=2. UPDATE_BELIEF: Packing increased duration 7.6us->11.0us and dropped speedup 79.3x->78.0x; amortization didn't help because grid was already small and per-program work doubled register pressure (70->80) without raising occupancy (still 2.08%). PERF_GAP: expected 1.30x, observed ~0.98x; reason: kernel is launch+latency bound at tiny N, packing serializes work per SM rather than spreading. next bet: revert packing (TOKENS_PER_PROG=1) and instead try (a) loading gate via constexpr cached path / fp16 math to cut regs, or (b) precompute expert routing in a tiny prelude to skip dead branches.

kernel_summary: Fused MoE forward with tiny shapes (B=1,S=16,D=32,I=32,E=8,top_k=1) in fp16: gate linear -> softmax -> top-1 expert -> SwiGLU MLP (W1,W3,W2) per token weighted by gate prob. Reference does per-expert Python loop + sort + scatter; the problem is dominated by kernel-launch and intermediate-allocation overhead, not compute or bandwidth. All weights (~50KB) fit in shared memory and the whole problem fits in a single CTA, so the dominant optimization is aggressive fusion into 1 (or 2) Triton kernel(s) that bypass the sort/scatter (unnecessary at top_k=1) and run gate+MLP end-to-end. Key constraints: tl.dot tile minimum (m=16), small-D matmul shapes, fp16 inputs with fp32 accumulation for softmax stability.
open_questions: Does the actual benchmark use defaults (dim=32,intermediate=32,E=8) as the docstring claims, or the values in __init__ signature defaults (also 32/32/8) — confirm shapes.
Will tl.dot accept (1,32)x(32,32) for the per-token program, or must we pad/broadcast to M=16?
Is fp32 accumulation needed in matmuls for tolerance, or is fp16 accum sufficient (faster on Blackwell at 420 TFLOPS)?
What output zeroing semantics matter — does the test allow a non-zero initialized output buffer (we can write all rows since top_k=1)?
Does the benchmark warmup amortize launch overhead enough that compute matters, or is steady-state still launch-dominated?
Is the gate bias absent (Linear(bias=False)) — confirmed, so we just need a single matmul for gate.
Will softmax be needed at all if we only need argmax + max-prob? (argmax of softmax == argmax of logits; weight requires actual softmax probability of the top class — yes needed.)
Numerical tolerance: does the eval use atol/rtol loose enough to allow fp16 softmax, or must we keep fp32 in the gate path?
